EU4 is my favorite. I played EU3, CK2 and Vic2 before. EU4 is a very well designed game that fixed many of the late game problems that EU3 had. It also keeps improving with each piece of added content and free patches. At this point I'm kind of concerned about the future of that franchise, because EU5 is going to either be stripped of features and thus go like Civ 5 did, or it will take entirely too long and be much too expensive to develop up front. The only hope is that they manage to reuse most of what they did in EU4 on a new engine.

As for why I like it over the others, it's the one I played the most, it's the most polished and the 1444 start also feels the most balanced. Although CK2 Dynasty Simulator is a fun game, it's a little bit too random and soap opera-ish. When it comes to the Victorian period, it feels like most of history already happened and the time frame is too short, the geopolitics much to locked in to do anything really interesting. Basically every game of Vic2 is a long, painful lead-up to WW1 and that makes it far too static compared to EU4 for my tastes. EU4 strikes a good balance between those extremes (well, technically HOI 3 would be the extreme but I haven't played it).

I really like EU4s updates too; especially the addition of Forts. It made steppe nations more realistic and less OP. Development is great too. In terms of Victoria 2, while I agree it can be a bit static, it is, as you said, true to the time period, and roleplay is one of the reasons I like Paradox's grand strategies. In response to your concerns about the future of the franchise, EU4 did come out relatively recently, and Paradox does tend to cycle their games. In fact, I believe HOI4 is currently in development. Basically I'm saying it'll be a while before EU5, touch wood, and that'll be plenty of time for technology and ideas to develop.

Victoria II !! Yes it's long but if you want GRAND strategy, this is like an rpg where you start with no weapons and maybe a potato sack. You build nations and have so, so many different ways to play. Also, it's not like other games with a difficulty setting and balancers, some nations are at such a huge disadvantage, they are very unlikely to be major players. Others are massive blind that may very well be able to have world domination. Little choice like what factory to build, what General to use, when to attack, etc make every game interesting.

It has a steep learning curve, but I love it.
